approach: Record the branch checked out at dispatch in a new optional field `dispatch_branch` on the `athena.job/1` record, which run/mod.rs already builds and commits at dispatch (the `Job` literal at ~888 must name every field, so that file cannot be skipped). Add a small `Dispatched` enum (`Unknown`, `Branch(name)`, `Detached`) to land.rs and give `land::plan` a `&Dispatched` argument. As its first step, `plan` reads `git.current_branch()`. If the dispatch branch is known and differs, `plan` returns `Plan::Stale` with a reason naming the dispatch branch, before the ancestor check. Both callers pass the value from the job record (`ctx.job.job` in `land_or_block`, `job.job` in `retry_landing`). First landing already turns Stale into a `stale` outcome (close.rs:229-256). Retry already bails with the job left blocked (close.rs:485-487). Records lacking the field map to `Unknown` and keep today's behavior. A detached dispatch is stored as `Some("")` and always goes stale. Tests: unit tests on `plan` in land.rs, round-trip tests in records.rs, and integration tests in lifecycle.rs using the existing `Scenario.during_verification` hook. The refused first landing still commits its stale outcome records on the checked-out branch; criterion 1 is tested as 'no job content lands, only records/ changes', and the plan asks the user to confirm that wording.

decisions.choice: Store the dispatch branch as `dispatch_branch: Option<String>` on `records::Job`, with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, set in run/mod.rs where the `Job` literal is built (line 888). `Some("")` means dispatched on a detached HEAD.
decisions.reason: No existing dispatch-time field holds the branch: `Outcome.branch` (records.rs ~872) is written at finish, and `Job.base_commit` is a commit id. The `Job` record is committed before any work starts (run/mod.rs:930-938) and both landing paths already hold it. `default` plus `skip_serializing_if` follow the existing `pin` field, so old records parse under `deny_unknown_fields` and new ones round-trip. `None` keeps old jobs on old behavior, as the assumptions require. run/mod.rs has to change because the `Job` literal lists every field; the reading's deliverables did not name it, but the build cannot succeed without it.

rejected.why: It is the branch at finish, which is the value to compare against, not the dispatch branch.

rejected.option: Add the field to the candidate record
rejected.why: Candidate has /1 and /2 schemas with parse rules in `AnyRecord::parse` and is written after the producer runs, not at dispatch.
A detached dispatch could not be told from a job dispatched before this change, which must keep the old behavior.

rejected.option: Derive the branch from git state at verification start
rejected.why: The branch can change between dispatch and verification, and a blocked retry runs in a later session. Only a record written at dispatch survives both.

rejected.option: Keep run/mod.rs out of the change by filling the field some other way (for example in store.rs)
rejected.why: The `Job` struct literal at run/mod.rs:888 must name the new field to compile, and the value must be read at dispatch, where that literal is built.

decisions.choice: Put the rule inside `land::plan` as its first step, with a new `&Dispatched` parameter. `plan` reads the current branch itself with `git.current_branch()`.
decisions.reason: close.rs:228 and :484 are the only callers of `plan` (grep of close.rs and crates), so one rule covers both. Reading the branch inside `plan`, from the repository that supplies `head`, stops a caller from passing a branch that disagrees with `head`. Both callers already hold the repository lock.

rejected.option: Check in each caller in close.rs
rejected.why: The rule would be written twice and could drift; it is not the root-cause location.

rejected.option: Caller passes the current branch as a string
rejected.why: It lets a caller or test pass a branch that is not the one `head` came from.

decisions.choice: A detached dispatch is always stale. A branch dispatch that finishes on a detached HEAD is also stale. The reason text says which case it is.
decisions.reason: The accepted assumption says a differing or absent branch is stale. A detached HEAD names no branch to compare, so the rule cannot confirm the job is landing where it started.

rejected.option: Land when both dispatch and finish are detached and the base is an ancestor
rejected.why: That is today's wrong behavior for the one case the rule cannot verify.

decisions.choice: Refuse with the existing outcome handling: `Plan::Stale` becomes a `stale` outcome on first landing, and a bail with the job left blocked on retry.
decisions.reason: Both are existing, tested outcomes for other stale reasons. Stale is chosen on first landing because a job that finished on another branch has no clean place to wait. A 'blocked' outcome there would also be committed on the checked-out branch (close.rs:321-331), where a later retry on the dispatch branch cannot see it. Writing records to a branch other than the checked-out one would be auto-switching, which is out of scope. On retry the job is already blocked and the bail leaves it so (close.rs:485-487), so it can still land after the user returns to the dispatch branch.

rejected.option: Leave the first-landing job blocked so it can be retried on the dispatch branch
rejected.why: The blocked record would be written to the checked-out branch (close.rs:321-331), where a retry on the dispatch branch cannot see it, and the retry path reads the landing state from the branch being retried on.

rejected.option: Write the stale records on the dispatch branch
rejected.why: It needs a write to a branch that is not checked out, which is auto-switching and out of scope.

rejected.option: Refuse without recording anything on the checked-out branch
rejected.why: The job would have no closing record and the run would look unfinished; it would also change how close.rs records outcomes, beyond the landing decision.

decisions.choice: No refusal-corpus case, and `refusal_corpus` is not a demonstration.
decisions.reason: The rule compares a stored branch name with the current one. It parses no request text, reading or stem list, so `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs` has no input form that maps to it.

rejected.why: The corpus covers reading and request text, and no such input reaches this rule.

decisions.reason: Its `athena.job/1` row (line 92) is not an exhaustive field list (the existing optional `pin` and `class_of_work` fields are not in it), and nothing in the repository tests it against the struct. Leaving it out keeps the change inside the listed deliverables plus the two files the change cannot do without (run/mod.rs, the lifecycle tests). The field is documented by its doc comment in records.rs.

rejected.why: It widens scope to a file outside the deliverables for a row that is already partial.

Pass `Dispatched::from_record(...)` from the job record to `plan` in `land_or_block` and `retry_landing`.

Set `dispatch_branch` in the dispatch-time `Job` literal (~888). Not a listed deliverable, but the literal names every field, so the field cannot be added without it, and dispatch is the only place the dispatch branch is known.
Add `dispatch_branch: Option<String>` to `Job`; update the test literal; add round-trip tests.

steps: Read before editing: land.rs `plan` and its tests, the `Job` struct in records.rs (~603-630), the `Job` literal in run/mod.rs (~888), the two `plan` calls in close.rs (228, 484), and lifecycle.rs `local_edits_block_the_landing_and_go_retries_it` (~1773) and `a_candidate_lands_over_a_records_only_interleave`.

In records.rs, add `dispatch_branch: Option<String>` to `Job` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` and a doc comment: the branch checked out at dispatch; `Some("")` means a detached HEAD; absent means a record made before the field.

Fix every `Job` struct literal: records.rs test (~4850) and store.rs `dispatched()` (~597) get `dispatch_branch: None`. In run/mod.rs, next to `dispatched_at` (885), call `self.git.current_branch()?` and set `dispatch_branch: Some(name or String::new())` in the literal.

In land.rs, add `pub enum Dispatched { Unknown, Branch(String), Detached }` with `from_record(Option<&str>)` (None gives Unknown, empty gives Detached). Add `dispatched: &Dispatched` to `plan`. As its first step read `git.current_branch()?` and return `Plan::Stale` with: a differing branch gives 'the job was dispatched on branch `A`, but branch `B` is checked out; nothing landed'; a detached current HEAD gives '... but HEAD is detached'; a detached dispatch gives 'the job was dispatched on a detached HEAD, which names no branch to land on'. `Unknown` skips the check. Update the header comment with the rule that the current branch must equal the dispatch branch, beside the ancestor rule, and note the detached and pre-field cases for an outside reader.

In close.rs, compute `Dispatched::from_record(ctx.job.job.as_ref().and_then(|j| j.dispatch_branch.as_deref()))` once before the attempts loop in `land_or_block` and pass it to `plan`; do the same from `job.job` in `retry_landing`.

Add the CHANGELOG entry under `## [Unreleased]` in a `### Changed` section (create it if absent), written for an outside reader: jobs now land only on the branch they were dispatched from; a job finished on another branch goes stale.

Add tests. land.rs: update the existing `plan` tests to pass `&Dispatched::Unknown`; add tests for a different branch (stale, reason names the dispatch branch, checked before the ancestor rule), the same branch with head equal to the base, the same branch after an excluded-path commit (`PRIVATE.md`, replay), detached dispatch, detached current HEAD (`git checkout --detach`), and `Unknown` landing as before. records.rs: the round-trip tests for criterion 7. lifecycle.rs: the criterion 1 and 3 tests and the extra criterion 2 assertions, with the hook capturing `other`'s tip through an `Arc<Mutex<String>>`.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any existing test that dispatched on one branch and finished on another, with a comment, and report which ones changed.

demonstrations.method: New integration test `a_job_finished_on_another_branch_is_stale_and_does_not_land` in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs. The fixture is on `main`; the job is asked and dispatched there. A `Scenario.during_verification` hook, guarded to fire once, runs `git checkout -q -b other` with no start point, so `other` starts at the current tip (the dispatch commit, which holds job.json and contains the base). The hook stores `other`'s tip in an `Arc<Mutex<String>>` it captured. `athena.go` then runs the real flow. The test asserts the finished state is `Stale` and the reason names `main`. It asserts what the agreed wording of criterion 1 means: `other`'s new tip has the captured tip as its parent, `git diff --name-only <captured tip> <new tip>` lists only paths under `records/`, README.md has no greeting, and `fingerprint(new tip, base)` equals `fingerprint(base, base)`. It also asserts `main`'s tip is unchanged, and that `job.json` at the dispatch commit has `dispatch_branch` equal to `main`. A land.rs unit test `a_job_dispatched_elsewhere_is_stale_on_another_branch` covers `plan` directly.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_job_finished_on_another_branch && cargo test --locked -p athena-core land::tests::a_job_dispatched
demonstrations.observes: The outcome is `stale` with a reason naming the dispatch branch. The checked-out branch gains no job content (only a records-only commit, which is how every stale outcome is recorded), and the dispatch branch tip does not move. In the unit test, `plan` returns `Plan::Stale` with the dispatch branch in the reason although the base is an ancestor of the head.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `plan` returns `Plan::Tree` because the base is an ancestor of `other`'s head. The job lands on `other`, the state is `Landed`, and the assertions on state, reason, README and fingerprint fail.

A new land.rs unit test `a_job_lands_when_the_dispatch_branch_is_checked_out` calls `plan` with `Dispatched::Branch("main")` on `main`, once with head equal to the base (expects `Plan::Tree` of the candidate's tree) and once after a commit that changes only an excluded path (`PRIVATE.md`, excluded by the test repo's `.gitattributes`), which takes the `merge_tree` replay branch and also expects `Plan::Tree`.

demonstrations.method: New integration test `a_blocked_job_will_not_retry_on_another_branch` in lifecycle.rs. It copies the setup of `local_edits_block_the_landing_and_go_retries_it`: `during_verification` writes a local edit, so `go` ends `Blocked` on `main`. The test restores README.md, runs `git checkout -q -b other`, and calls `athena.go` on the job again, which reaches `retry_landing` (close.rs:387). It asserts the call returns an error that names `main` and says the job stays blocked, that `other`'s tip is unchanged by the retry (the retry bail writes nothing, close.rs:485-487), that README.md has no greeting, and that there is no `outcome-landed.json`. It then checks out `main`, runs `go` again, and asserts `Landed`.
demonstrations.observes: The retry on the wrong branch is refused with the dispatch branch in the error, the job stays blocked and nothing is committed. The retry on the dispatch branch lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check in `plan`, the retry on `other` lands the change: `go` returns `Ok` with state `Landed`, so the `is_err` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Athena::go` on a blocked job (reaching `retry_landing`) and `land::plan`. The fixture and hook exist today; `local_edits_block_the_landing_and_go_retries_it` already uses them. The new test adds no seam.
